Product Name: Solifenacin Succinate Tablets BP 5 mg Film coated tablets 5 mg

components.content:
The manufacturing process for Solifenacin Succinate Tablets BP 5 mg involves several key stages, starting with the
precise weighing and dispensing of all raw materials. This is followed by the dry mixing of the active pharmaceutical
ingredient (API), diluents, and binder. Wet granulation is then performed by adding the binder solution. The resultant
granules are dried and subsequently sized to achieve the desired particle distribution. Lubrication is carried out by
adding magnesium stearate before the core tablets are compressed. Finally, the compressed tablets undergo film
coating with a suspension containing Readycoat Iron Oxide Yellow, followed by drying of the coated tablets. The
finished product is then inspected and packaged.

components.content:
The manufacturing process for Solifenacin Succinate Tablets BP 5 mg is a multi-stage operation designed to ensure
product quality and consistency. Initially, all raw materials, including Solifenacin Succinate, Lactose Monohydrate,
Maize Starch, Hypromellose, and Magnesium Stearate, are accurately weighed and dispensed according to the
validated batch formula. The API, diluents, and binder (Maize Starch) are then subjected to dry mixing in a V-Blender
or Rapid Mixer Granulator (RMG) to ensure homogeneity. Subsequently, wet granulation is performed in the RMG by
adding a binder solution prepared with Hypromellose and Purified Water. The wet mass is then dried in a Fluid Bed
Dryer (FBD) to achieve the specified Loss on Drying (LOD). The dried granules are milled to obtain a uniform
particle size distribution. Following milling, Magnesium Stearate is added for lubrication in a V-Blender. The
lubricated blend is then compressed into core tablets using a Rotary Tablet Press. The core tablets are subsequently
film-coated in a Coating Pan using a suspension of Readycoat Iron Oxide Yellow in Purified Water. The coated tablets
are dried to ensure proper film formation. Finally, the finished tablets undergo visual inspection for any defects and
are then packaged into ALU/ALU blister packs.
